A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ActINR work. Their complete main texts, supplementary material, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original video interpolation, inpainting, denoising, super-resolution and regression results, alongside ablations and failure-case analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds resolution, runtime, motion-filtering and compression results in its supplement.

M1.justification: The architecture, training objective and Eqs. (1)–(3) remain unchanged. V2 adds limited application procedures: temporal median filtering of learned biases for motion suppression, and pruning with 8-bit post-quantization for compression.

E1.justification: The original UVG/DAVIS tasks and videos are retained. V2 extends coverage with explicit compression evaluation on Bosphorus and a vibrating-tuning-fork motion-filtering example, without broadly replacing or expanding the original benchmarks.

E2.justification: The new compression comparison evaluates JPEG2000 and Hybrid NeRV against ActINR (Fig. 16). Hybrid NeRV is distinct from the H-NeRV Boost comparator retained in the original experiments. Comparator membership in Tables 1–5 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Added evaluations introduce 4K-versus-HD interpolation conditions, encoding-time and decoding-FPS measurements, and rate-distortion testing with pruning and 8-bit post-quantization. Previously stated protocols remain intact; the newly disclosed model sizes do not establish that existing experiments changed.

E4.justification: V2 adds a resolution robustness check on four UVG videos (Table 6) and a targeted bias–motion case study using median filtering (Fig. 15). Existing activation, interpolation, GOP-size, patch-size and parameter-count ablations, plus the patch-boundary failure and remedy, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–5 and existing plotted results are unchanged. V2 adds 4K/HD scores, runtime results including ActINR's 5h19m encoding and 59.28 FPS decoding, qualitative motion suppression, and a compression curve placing ActINR above JPEG2000 but below Hybrid NeRV. These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Eqs. (1)–(3), and assumptions motivating shared weights and moving compact basis functions are retained. V2 introduces no new formal definitions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution summary and conclusion retain the same central claims about bias-modulated continuous video representation and its video-processing capabilities. The added compression qualification concerns applicability rather than redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5 and the supplement newly acknowledge that Hybrid NeRV performs better on compression and position ActINR primarily for inverse problems. V2 also interprets the resolution and filtering results as evidence of resolution resilience and a bias–motion relationship. The existing patch-boundary limitation remains.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents the 3-million-parameter FF-NeRV reproduction, approximately triple ActINR capacity for inpainting, batched window evaluation, and initialization from the preceding group's weights. These supplement v1's existing hyperparameters and hardware information; they do not establish changes to previously reported runs.

R1.justification: The cited-work list is unchanged. However, the new compression discussion substantively refines positioning relative to Hybrid NeRV: ActINR emphasizes inverse problems while acknowledging Hybrid NeRV's compression advantage.

P1.justification: V2 makes grammatical and author-text corrections, condenses the limitations paragraph, and adds supplementary subsections. The main section order, narrative and most wording remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 6–7 and Figures 15–16, with local supplementary-page reflow and continuous pagination. Original Tables 1–5 and Figures 1–14 are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful evidence about resolution robustness, speed, motion filtering and compression, while disclosing previously missing implementation and model-capacity details. Acknowledging Hybrid NeRV's compression advantage makes the applicability discussion more balanced. These gains improve transparency and practical assessment, but remain limited additions to otherwise unchanged central evidence.
